newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus launches new A340 models.
newsitem.headline: Airbus launches new A340 models.

text.p: Airbus Industrie managing director Jean Pierson announced on Sunday at the Paris airshow that the European aircraft consortium was launching two new versions of its A340 four-engine wide-body airliner.

The commercial launch was for the longer-range A340-500 and the larger-capacity 378-seat A340-600, Pierson told a news conference at the Paris air show. Total investment would be $2.5 billion for the project, he said.

Given the costs involved, it was "mandatory to seek a launch customer for this programme," Pierson said. Although the commercial launch was being announced today, he hoped the industrial launch could be made in September, once an airline customer had signed up.
The new jets will initially be powered by Rolls Royce Trent 500 engines, developing thrust of around 56,000 pounds.

"A decisive factor" in selecting Rolls-Royce was that "their offer is not on exclusive terms," Pierson said. That left it open for a second company to bid for engine contracts, but there were conditions to be met, he added. He did not specify what the conditions were.

Airbus had also been looking at the Pratt & Whitney PW4500 engine for the new planes, after failing to get the price discounts it wanted from General Electric Aircraft Engines during a period of exclusive negotiations.

The A340-600 is a stop-gap product aimed at attacking Boeing's monopoly of the high-capacity market with its 777 giant twinjet and the 747 jumbo jet. In the longer term, Airbus wants to launch its A3XX 500-seater to overtake the 747.

In a statement, Pierson said Airbus selected the Trent 500 because of its low noise, high fuel efficiency and low operating costs. "It offers the market the best technical and commercial combination together with the greatest flexibility," he said.

The A340-600 will be ready for passenger service in Autumn, 2001. Airbus said the plane "is an attractive replacement for early model Boeing 747s, offering a similar size but significantly better direct operating costs and trip costs than the 747-400, as well as more range".
The A340-600 will feature a larger wing and stretched body to provide the additional capacity.

The A340-500 will be similar to the 600 model but with a shorter fuselage and more range. It will carry 313 passengers and will be able to fly non-stop from London to Perth, making it the world's longest range airliner, Airbus said.
